function: Multi-agent RL jointly allocating beam illumination (beam hopping), bandwidth and transmit power of a multi-beam GEO satellite, to maximize throughput, minimize delay and keep delay fairness (p. 6).
system: GEO multi-beam satellite forward link with phased-array antenna, 33 cells with 7 beams and 109 cells with 23 beams, 500 MHz bandwidth, 20 GHz Ka-band, no RIS (p. 9).
method: Multi-agent PPO-based actor-critic: traffic-aware attention encoder as critic, sequential multi-step decoder as actor, Stackelberg Markov game; reinforcement learning trained offline, 2,500,000 steps (p. 10).
data_channel: Own simulator: Bessel beam-gain pattern, rain, cloud and gas attenuation, Poisson traffic arrivals; parameters partly taken from [9]; no standardized channel model, dataset or measurements (p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained offline per scenario (33-7, 109-23); tested over traffic 500-3000 Mbps; pre-trained policy applied to 6, 8, 9 beams with 0-100% of training steps (Table VI, p. 11).
baselines: Non-learned: R-SRA (random), P-SRA (periodic), MB-SRA (max buffer), GA-SRA (genetic). Learned: PPO-SRA, MAPPO-SRA, DDQN [9], DeepMBS [13] (p. 9).
metrics: Long-term throughput (Mbps), response delay (ms), maximum-minimum delay gap (ms), episode reward, time cost per decision (p. 12).
complexity: Order O(sum over layers of w_{l-1} w_l (N k^2 + k^2)) (Eq. 36), compared with baselines; measured time cost about 26 microseconds per decision (Table IX, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 9: "The simulation parameters are presented in Table III, incorporating some information from [9]" - own simulator (Bessel beam gain, rain/cloud/gas attenuation, p. 4); no 3GPP TR 38.811, DeepMIMO or measured data. DVB-S2 [31] is cited only for the system (p. 4).
q2_support: p. 11: "applying pre-trained policies to new scenarios with" limited data; Table VI tests 33-6, 33-8 and 33-9 (other beam numbers than 33-7) at 0%, 1%, 5%, 10% and 100% of the training steps.
q3_support: p. 9: "satellite resource allocation algorithms, including rule-based," heuristic and RL methods: R-SRA, P-SRA, MB-SRA, GA-SRA (non-learned) and PPO-SRA, MAPPO-SRA, DDQN [9], DeepMBS [13] (learned), compared on throughput, delay and delay fairness (Figs. 6-8, pp. 10-11).
q4_support: p. 12: "Thus, the overall time complexity of" our proposed TAMS method is the big-O expression of Eq. (36); Table IX lists the same order and a measured time cost of about 26 microseconds.
q5_support: p. 9: "The simulation parameters are presented in Table III, incorporating some information from [9]" - own simulated data; no code or data link, DOI or availability statement in pp. 1-13, and no public or measured dataset.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Area 6: learned control of beams, bandwidth and power in a satellite link counts as physical layer, although beam hopping also schedules beams over cells. Table III gives a 20 GHz Ka-band link while the text states a 0.15 m wavelength (p. 9). The ablation heading 'number of users' (p. 11) refers to beam numbers. q1 = 0: DVB-S2 [31] is cited for the system model only, and the atmospheric attenuation formulas (p. 4) carry no ITU-R or 3GPP reference; the reviewer may confirm. Baselines were re-implemented by the authors (p. 10). Tables III-IX and Figs. 5-8 read from the page images.
